issues.legal_issue: A civil court hearing a land-acquisition compensation reference cannot dismiss the reference for the claimant’s default.
material_facts: Land was acquired and, after objecting to the compensation awarded, the landowner obtained a reference to a civil court for determination of the objection.
When the reference was taken up, neither the claimant nor counsel appeared, and the civil court dismissed the reference for default.
The governing procedure required the civil court to determine the objection and make an award.
issues.conclusion: The dismissal for default was set aside, and the civil court was directed to proceed to determine the reference and make an award.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 18 and 20 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, require a properly referred objection to be determined by the civil court; Section 26 requires the court’s award to be in writing and treats it as a decree. A party’s non-participation may put that party at risk of an adverse award, but does not empower the court to dismiss the reference for default. The Court relied on Abdul Kareem v. State of M.P., Munda v. Oraon, Sanai v. State, Joseph v. Government of Kerala, and Jogi Sahu v. Collector. Jogi Sahu also supports entertaining an application to restore a reference under Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure, even where the application cites Order 9 Rule 9.

predicates.compensation_reference_pending: A landowner’s objection to compensation was referred by the acquiring authority to a civil court for determination.
predicates.court_required_to_determine_objection_an: The procedure governing the reference required the civil court to determine the objection and make an award.
predicates.claimant_and_counsel_absent: The claimant and the claimant’s counsel did not appear when the civil court took up the reference.
predicates.reference_not_dismissible_for_default: The civil court cannot dismiss the compensation reference merely because the claimant did not appear.

issues.definition: When a compensation reference is pending, the court is required to determine the objection and make an award, and the claimant and counsel are absent, the reference cannot be dismissed for default.
